deep.reconstruction:
Context: magnetic inclination (dip) observations made with an inclinatorium (dip circle) using two needles, Nro 3 and Nro 4. 'B Nord' means pole B of the needle points north. The date is 1842 May 10. The heading '90° 30'' is probably the circle or azimuth setting (my reading). Circle readings near 112° and 111° stand for 180° minus the dip, i.e. supplementary readings from the other circle or needle position. Readings near 67° are direct.

LEFT (pencil, raw data). Each setting has two vernier or needle-end readings.
- Needle 4: (112°20', 112°17' | 67°54', 67°55'), (112°21'30", 112°21'30" | 67°56', 67°56'), (112°17'30", 112°19' | 67°55', 67°55'), (112°18'30", 112°17' | 67°53'30", 67°52'30").
- Needle 3: (67°16', 67°17' | 111°57', 111°56'30"), (67°14', 67°15' | 111°52', 111°51'30"), (67°15', 67°18' | 111°49', 111°50'), (67°13', 67°15'30" | 111°48', 111°50').
- Bottom left: '26.25 / 12.25' with a brace. Meaning unclear, perhaps times or temperatures.

RIGHT (ink, reduction).
(1) The ink entries are the means of each pencil pair. Example: (112°20' + 112°17')/2 = 112°18'30" and (67°54' + 67°55')/2 = 67°54'30".
- Needle 4 pairs: (112°18'30", 67°54'30"), (112°21'30", 67°56'), (112°18'15", 67°55'), (112°18'45", 67°53').
- Means of the four: 112°19'15" and 67°54'37.5".
- Reduction (my explicit step): [(180° − 112°19'15") + 67°54'37.5"]/2 = (67°40'45" + 67°54'37.5")/2 = 67°47'41.25". Gauss labels this '−b': it still contains a needle correction b to be subtracted.
(2) Needle 3 pairs: (67°16'30", 111°56'45"), (67°14'30", 111°50'45"), (67°16'30", 111°49'30"), (67°14'15", 111°49').
- Means: 67°15'26.25" and 111°51'30".
- Reduction: [67°15'26.25" + (180° − 111°51'30")]/2 = (67°15'26.25" + 68°8'30")/2 = 67°41'58.125", labeled '−a'.
(3) Determining the corrections a and b.
- Today's difference: 67°47'41.25" − 67°41'58.125" = 5'43.125" = b − a.
- A second value, b − a = 5'1.875", comes from another series not on this page.
- Two values of a + b: 14'52.5" and 13'52.5". Their origin is presumably the reversed-pole (A Nord) series. Note that 13'52.5" equals 67°54'37.5" − 67°40'45" from block (1); that may be a coincidence.
- Means: a + b = 14'22.5" and b − a = 5'22.5".
- Hence b = (14'22.5" + 5'22.5")/2 = 9'52.5" and a = (14'22.5" − 5'22.5")/2 = 4'30".
(4) Corrected dips.
- Needle 3: 67°41'58.125" − 4'30" = 67°37'28.125".
- Needle 4: 67°47'41.25" − 9'52.5" = 67°37'48.75".
- Both appear in the right-hand column of minutes.
- Two columns of four determinations (degrees 67 understood):
  - Left column: 36'58", 36'20.625", 36'0", 37'28". Mean 36'41.65625", labeled 'Nadel 3'.
  - Right column: 37'28.125", 36'41.25", 36'30", 37'48.75". Mean 37'7.03125", labeled 'Nadel 4'.
- Mean of the two needles: 67°36'54.34375", attributed to the mean epoch 1842 May 5½.
- Compared with the earlier result 67°42'52.6" for 1841 Oct 4¼, this shows the secular decrease of the Göttingen dip, about 6' in 7 months.

Purpose: routine reduction of absolute inclination measurements at Göttingen. Averaging over circle and needle reversals cancels the collimation and graduation errors. Pole-reversal-type corrections a and b remove each needle's centre-of-gravity error. The result is a mean dip for monitoring secular variation.
errors: Two ink means seem to differ by exactly 1' from the pencil raw pairs as I read them. Needle 4, 4th pair: (112°18'30" + 112°17')/2 = 112°17'45", but the ink has 112°18'45". Needle 3, 2nd pair: (111°52' + 111°51'30")/2 = 111°51'45", but the ink has 111°50'45". The pencil is faint, so these may be misreadings of the pencil rather than slips by Gauss.
All other arithmetic checks exactly: the means, the half-sums, a, b, the needle means 36'41.65625" and 37'7.03125", and the overall 36'54.34375".
Why needle 3's corrected value 37'28.125" sits in the 'Nadel 4' (right) column, while the left column has 37'28.000", cannot be resolved from this page. The column labels are taken as written.

results.what: Reduction of dip-circle readings: averaging direct and supplementary (180°−x) readings over circle and needle reversals for two needles.
results.modern_name: Absolute magnetic inclination measurement with a dip circle (reversal method)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-19th c. practice (Mayer, Gambey, Humboldt, Sabine)

results.what: Separation of the needle corrections a and b by solving the sum and difference equations a+b and b−a, each from averaged series.
results.modern_name: Elimination of centre-of-gravity / needle error by pole reversal; solving a 2x2 linear system

results.what: Comparison of mean dip 1842 May 5½ (67°36'54") with 1841 Oct 4¼ (67°42'53").
results.usually_credited_to: Göttingen Magnetic Union observations (Gauss, Weber); Gauss-Weber Resultate

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observational reduction of magnetic dip measurements from the Göttingen magnetic programme. The methods are standard instrumental practice, and Gauss's involvement in such measurements is well documented.

checkable.asserts: Mean of the 112° minutes for needle 4 is 19.25' (112°19'15"); should be 0.
Mean of the 67° minutes for needle 4 is 54.625' (54'37.5"); should be 0.
Needle 3 mean of the 67° readings is 15'26.25"; should be 0.
Needle 3 mean of the 111° readings is 51.5'; should be 0.
Needle 3 half-sum gives 67°41'58.125" (in arcseconds); should be 0.
b − a from today's data is 5'43.125"; should be 0.

transcription_corrections: The right-hand entries '5 1,875' and '5 43.125' are values of b−a (5'1.875" and 5'43.125"); the large 'b−a' label belongs to them.
The final line likely reads '67. 42. 52,6' (67°42'52.6") for 1841 Oct 4¼.
Bottom-left pencil, Nro 4 4th pair: the second reading is read as '17' (112°17'). The ink mean 112°18'45" suggests it may instead be '19'.
Nro 3 2nd pair, 111° readings: '111.52 / 51.30' gives the mean 51'45", whereas the ink has 50'45". One of the faint pencil readings may be misread.
